clue.text: Ribs gunners wed, perhaps

parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so 'ribs' is old slang for wives; these are wives that soldiers married in wartime

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about soldiers' ribs, as if gunners were marrying bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribs' looks anatomical, but it is jocular slang for wives, after the Genesis story of Eve made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who married serving soldiers during a conflict, gunners being artillerymen, are known by this phrase.

clue.text: Maid known, perhaps, to be included in this

definitions.text: Maid known, perhaps, to be included in this

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words maid known may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A maid known to be part of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MAID KNOWN; as an &lit, a maid is indeed part of the female sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Women as a whole, the female sex, naturally includes every maid.

clue.text: Stuff to rub bows and even parts of arrows in

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of the word arrows are taken: second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Archery gear: something to rub on bows, and arrows to put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bows' suggests archery with the arrows, but means violin bows. 'even parts of' picks R, O, S from arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists rub resin onto their bow hair to make it grip the strings.

clue.text: Indication of what's ahead, by the way

definitions.meaning: a notice warning drivers of what is coming
read literally: placed beside the road

explanation.surface: Someone mentions, incidentally, a hint of what is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway phrase meaning incidentally, but read literally it describes a notice by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic signage warns motorists of bends ahead and stands at the roadside.

clue.text: Handing over — a sixth of it

definitions.meaning: the act of handing something over, as of goods
'it' is a cricket over, which has six balls bowled

explanation.surface: Handing something over, but only one sixth of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over consists of six balls, each one bowled being this.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing goods over is this, and in cricket each of the six balls in an over is one.

clue.text: So many get excellent service in comfort

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

explanation.surface: Many people find excellent customer service a comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like customer care, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation in distress is a synonym for comfort.

clue.text: Hence Pythagoras, second prophet

parts.note: Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A note about Pythagoras and another prophetic figure following him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hence Pythagoras' means the place the philosopher came from: he was born on this Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island in the Aegean was the birthplace of the mathematician, so he came from there.

clue.text: "To — to seek, to find, and not to yield" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "To — to seek, to find, and not to yield" (Tennyson)

parts.words: "To — to seek, to find, and not to yield" (Tennyson)
parts.note: the closing line of Tennyson's poem Ulysses, with its first verb left blank to fill in

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tennyson with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses ends with the resolve to make great effort, seek, find and not yield.

clue.text: Hearty lot, perhaps, in important case

definitions.meaning: the hearts in bridge are one of the higher-ranking card groups
a weighty lawsuit

explanation.surface: Cheerful people involved in a significant legal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty lot' sounds like jolly people, but is the set of heart cards; in bridge, hearts and spades score higher.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, hearts rank as a senior card group; a weighty lawsuit is also this.

clue.text: At last a replacement in 6 ac in South Pacific

indicators.note: the final letter of the cross-referenced island is swapped for the letter a

parts.note: the answer to 6 across, the Greek island

explanation.surface: A replacement for the island at six across, located in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek island's final S is replaced by A, giving the Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polynesian island group lies in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Wrongly bid a spade? Not if you speak plainly

definitions.text: Wrongly bid a spade? Not if you speak plainly

parts.words: Wrongly bid a spade? Not if you speak plainly
parts.note: plain speakers 'call a spade a spade', so they never give it a wrong name; 'bid' also nods to calling in card games

explanation.surface: A bridge player's error of bidding spades, contrasted with blunt honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' suggests bridge, but the clue turns on the idiom 'call a spade a spade': only someone not speaking plainly names it wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To name something wrongly, or make an erroneous call in a game, is the verb here.

clue.text: Title lucky character gives novel

parts.note: Lord is a title of nobility
Lucky Jim is the hero of Kingsley Amis's comic novel, so the lucky character is Jim

explanation.surface: A fortunate person's peerage turning into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Joseph Conrad's novel; 'Lucky Jim' is a different novel, by Kingsley Amis.
explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's 1900 book about a disgraced seaman is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Clementine's footwear — standard for the well-dressed?

definitions.meaning: in the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' her shoes were number nine
the idiom 'dressed to the ...' means dressed as smartly as possible

explanation.surface: A question about Clementine's shoes and whether they set the standard for smart dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk song gives the girl shoe size nine, and immaculate dressers are said to be dressed to these.

clue.text: Contrariwise the story of Mr Bultitude

definitions.meaning: meaning the other way round
F. Anstey's 1882 comic novel in which Mr Bultitude swaps bodies with his schoolboy son

explanation.surface: A reader cites a Victorian comic novel while arguing the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means 'the other way about', and Anstey used it as the title of his body-swap novel.

clue.text: For example, 11 steering off course

indicators.note: a ship off course has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone steering off course, with eleven as a passing example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' rearranges STEERING. '11' is not a cross-reference here but the number eleven itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a whole number, an example of the set of numbers with no fractional part.

clue.text: Retiring, or giving up

definitions.meaning: going to bed for the night
handing over, as a criminal to the police

explanation.surface: A choice between retirement and surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving work, but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed is this phrasal verb, and so is surrendering someone or something to authorities.

clue.text: Easy thing to enter University, back in island

indicators.note: the whole assembled run is then read from its end to its start
the U goes into the middle of the easy thing, as a student enters a place

parts.note: something simple is 'as easy as ABC'

explanation.surface: Getting into university is easy, and then you return to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts U inside ABC to give ABUC, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean nation is a large island south of Florida.

clue.text: To the Israelites a blooming miracle

definitions.text: To the Israelites a blooming miracle

parts.words: To the Israelites a blooming miracle
parts.note: in Numbers 17 the staff of Moses' brother budded and blossomed overnight as a sign to the tribes

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a remarkable wonder for the Israelites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' looks like a mild British intensifier but is literal: the staff burst into flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The high priest's staff that sprouted blossoms and almonds is the biblical wonder meant.

clue.text: It reveals the basis for Rossini's opera

definitions.meaning: something that gives away a secret
Rossini's William Tell is based on the story of the Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A remark about the source of a Rossini opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway sign betrays secrets, and the legend of William Tell underlies Rossini's opera.

clue.text: Right under, might we infer from this remnant?

definitions.text: Right under, might we infer from this remnant?

parts.words: Right under, might we infer from this remnant?
parts.note: the opposite of right is left and the opposite of under is over, so the remnant's name inverts the clue's first two words

explanation.surface: A question about what we might deduce from a leftover scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right under' looks like a position, but each word is the opposite of a word in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remaining after use, such as uneaten food, is a remnant.

clue.text: Repair hole in 29

definitions.meaning: to mend a hole in knitted fabric by weaving thread across it
refers to the answer at 29 across, a mild curse

explanation.surface: Mending a hole in something numbered twenty-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: '29' is a cross-reference to 29 across, SWEARWORD; this word is a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sock-mending with yarn is this, and it is also a minced form of 'damn', a mild oath.

clue.text: He's always concerned with side-issues

parts.note: side-issues read as issues of picking a team side, as a cricket panel member does

explanation.surface: A person who obsesses over trivial matters away from the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-issues' sounds like trivial distractions, but here it means choosing a sports side.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who picks players for a national team is always deciding on the side.

clue.text: Current instance of educational division

definitions.meaning: a flow of water
a group of pupils of similar ability in a British school

explanation.surface: A present example of how schools divide pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but is a flowing body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a water current, and in British schools pupils are divided by ability into such groups.

clue.text: Prayer, in matins — name is out of place

indicators.note: the name letter shifts to another position within the word matins

parts.note: taken as written, the morning service

explanation.surface: A prayer said at morning service, with a name misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prayer' looks like a request to God, but it means one who prays: the insect holds its forelegs as if praying.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect holds its front legs folded as if at worship, hence one who prays.

clue.text: Tent-maker of Minnesota

definitions.meaning: the apostle worked as a tent-maker, according to Acts 18
the capital city of the US state of Minnesota

explanation.surface: A tent manufacturer based in Minnesota.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle earned his living making tents, and the Minnesota state capital bears his name.

clue.text: Pulls up this turf

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: draws means pulls, as a cart

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up a patch of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassy ground, a lawn, is an old word for an expanse of grass.

clue.text: Legend, in two parts, of the Roc (weight about a pound)

definitions.text: Legend, in two parts, of the Roc

indicators.note: the weight goes around the a and the pound, enclosing them

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A legend about the mythical Roc, split into two parts, with a weight mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Legend' as 'leg end': the end of the leg of the Roc, a giant mythical bird, is its claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw sits at the end of its leg, the cryptic sense of the split word.

clue.text: Young lady love given a whirl on the ranch

definitions.text: given a whirl on the ranch

parts.note: a lass is a young woman
love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman and her lover go dancing at a ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a whirl' suggests a dance or a try, but describes a cowboy's rope spun overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is spun around before being thrown at cattle.

clue.text: Grow a sort of nutmeg

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so these letters are sorted into another form

explanation.surface: Instructions to cultivate a variety of nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges A NUTMEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase or enlarge something is a verb synonym for making it bigger.

clue.text: Notice face saving device used by mentor

parts.note: an ad is a notice, as in an advertisement
a visor protects the face, literally saving it

explanation.surface: A mentor uses a notice and a face-saving trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saving' suggests avoiding embarrassment, but here it is literal protection for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is someone who gives counsel, a variant spelling of adviser.

clue.text: Sudden impulse to show this material

indicators.note: the letters are put on display within the words sudden impulse

explanation.surface: Someone has a sudden urge to show off this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-wearing cotton twill used for jeans is a fabric.

clue.text: What Pinafore's captain hardly ever used

definitions.text: What Pinafore's captain hardly ever used

parts.words: What Pinafore's captain hardly ever used
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, the captain claims he never uses a big, big D, 'well, hardly ever'

explanation.surface: A question about the habits of the captain of HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'big, big D' the captain avoids is 'damn', an oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain boasts he never utters an oath such as 'damn', then admits 'hardly ever'.
